question.text: 'Aravalli Impact Ventures AIF-II' is a Category I AIF (Social Impact Fund) targeting INR 500 crore. Ms. Neha Kulkarni, the manager, is setting the sponsor's continuing interest / GP commitment. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the MINIMUM sponsor/manager commitment requirement for a Category I/II AIF, and why do most managers voluntarily commit MORE?

answer.text: Minimum is 2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore (whichever is lower) for Category I/II — managers, including first-time managers, may voluntarily commit more to provide comfort and alignment of interest to investors
Minimum is 10% or INR 25 crore (lower of the two) — managers don't voluntarily exceed this
Minimum is 5% or INR 10 crore (higher of the two) — no voluntary excess
No minimum; entirely commercial negotiation with LPs

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the minimum sponsor/manager continuing interest for Category I/II AIFs is at least 2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is lower. The workbook also notes that sponsors and managers, particularly first-time managers, may voluntarily commit more to provide comfort and signal alignment of interest to investors. The Trap: 10%/INR 25 crore is not the prescribed minimum. 5%/INR 10 crore reverses the threshold and the lower-of test. 'No minimum' is incorrect — SEBI prescribes a floor. Note: Two ideas travel together — the regulatory floor (2.5% or INR 5 crore, lower of) and the voluntary higher commitment that managers may make to provide investor comfort.
